name: extract_stream
description: Extract one data stream of an NTFS volume by inode address to a file with icat (the Sleuth Kit). The stream is streamed straight to `output` (never held in memory and never printed). `output` is a file under work/<your id>/ (or work/extracted/<your id>/ or work/quarantine/<your id>/; run as a job, the harness gives a work/<your id>/... path to $OUT): any other place in the run, and anything under inputs/, is refused with the places named. Nothing already there is overwritten: a file at `output` refuses the call, and what a failed run keeps (<output>.partial, <output>.stderr) takes the next free name (.2, .3) so a second run never replaces what the first kept; the answer names the file it kept. The answer is what a reader cites: output path, size and sha256, image, offset in sectors, the inode address as asked and parsed (entry, attribute type, attribute id: 168 or 168-128-4 names a stream such as an alternate data stream), icat's exit status and its standard error whole in a file beside the output. A failed or timed-out icat leaves what it wrote as the .partial file and the answer says status failed (exit 1), never an extraction. The same contract as the base pack's icat_extract, without its image catalogue; read the stream with the tool that fits its type. SENSITIVE: a stream can hold a secret; the tool never prints it, and its size and sha256 are the custody record of the file. The program runs in the tool's own process group (never a session of its own), so the harness ending the tool ends it; the tool's own deadline kills it and what it started, and SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP do the same and the answer is then status interrupted.

image.description: Path to the disk image or volume icat can read (an E01 is read through the Sleuth Kit's libewf where it has it)

inode.description: Inode or inode-attribute address to extract, e.g. 168 or 168-128-4

offset.description: Volume offset in SECTORS (icat -o); 0 for a logical volume with no partition table

output.description: The file to write the stream to: work/<your id>/<name> (or work/extracted/<your id>/..., work/quarantine/<your id>/...); refused if it exists, lies under inputs/ or anywhere else in the run

timeout_seconds.description: How long to let icat run (default 240, at most 270)
